challenge.name: This Code's Got Bars!
challenge.description: 1-Dimensional and Patented! (barcode challenge). HARDWARE/on-site challenge: likely a 1-D barcode printed on the BSides Orlando 2026 badge or at the venue. REMOTE-ATTEMPT GUIDANCE: search for published badge artwork/design files or high-resolution photos of the badge and any barcode on it, then decode with zbarimg/dcode (try Code39, Code128, UPC, POSTNET, ITF). Also try the badge's PCB silkscreen. Flag format sun{...}.

records.findings_summary: Flag found via OSINT on published BSides Orlando 2026 badge hardware design files + 1-D barcode decode: downloaded the public badge repo github.com/badge-gallery/bsidesorlando-2026, found a Code-128 barcode layer inside hardware/uv_art.psd (layer named 'sun{ctf_r_4_h00m4n5}.png'), flattened it and decoded it with zbarimg -> CODE-128:sun{ctf_r_4_h00m4n5}.: sun{ctf_r_4_h00m4n5} | Evidence: GitHub search surfaced repo badge-gallery/bsidesorlando-2026 (BSides Orlando badge hardware/KiCad files) matching the BSides Orlando category. ; `grep -rao 'sun{[^}]*}' .` on the repo returned sun{ctf_r_4_h00m4n5} inside hardware/uv_art.psd. ; psd-tools enumerated uv_art.psd layers: 'bsbadgeE', 'sun{ctf_r_4_h00m4n5}.png' (bbox 1191,1153,1856,1281 = wide/short barcode), 'Copper Layer', 'LED Locations'. ; Extracted that layer (665x128) -> /challenge/workspace/layer_bars.png, flattened onto white -> layer_bars_flat.png. ; `zbarimg -q --raw layer_bars_flat.png` => sun{ctf_r_4_h00m4n5}; `zbarimg layer_bars_flat.png` => CODE-128:sun{ctf_r_4_h00m4n5} (symbology explicitly reported as CODE-128, a 1-D barcode = 'got bars').
solution_steps: 在 GitHub 上搜索 BSides Orlando 2026 badge，发现公开仓库 badge-gallery/bsidesorlando-2026（含 badge 硬件 KiCad/PSD 设计文件）。
克隆仓库并全仓库 grep flag 格式，在 hardware/uv_art.psd 中发现字符串 sun{ctf_r_4_h00m4n5}。
用 psd-tools 列出 PSD 图层，发现名为 'sun{ctf_r_4_h00m4n5}.png' 的图层，其包围盒 1191,1153–1856,1281 呈宽扁状，正是 1-D 条码。
导出该图层为 layer_bars.png，透明底合成到白底得 layer_bars_flat.png。
用 zbarimg 解码：输出 CODE-128:sun{ctf_r_4_h00m4n5}，与图层名一致，确认为本题（1-Dimensional 条码）flag。
evidence: GitHub search surfaced repo badge-gallery/bsidesorlando-2026 (BSides Orlando badge hardware/KiCad files) matching the BSides Orlando category.
`grep -rao 'sun{[^}]*}' .` on the repo returned sun{ctf_r_4_h00m4n5} inside hardware/uv_art.psd.
psd-tools enumerated uv_art.psd layers: 'bsbadgeE', 'sun{ctf_r_4_h00m4n5}.png' (bbox 1191,1153,1856,1281 = wide/short barcode), 'Copper Layer', 'LED Locations'.
Extracted that layer (665x128) -> /challenge/workspace/layer_bars.png, flattened onto white -> layer_bars_flat.png.
`zbarimg -q --raw layer_bars_flat.png` => sun{ctf_r_4_h00m4n5}; `zbarimg layer_bars_flat.png` => CODE-128:sun{ctf_r_4_h00m4n5} (symbology explicitly reported as CODE-128, a 1-D barcode = 'got bars').
Visual inspection of the enlarged layer confirms a 1-D vertical-bar barcode pattern.

NOTE: submit_flag's browser recipe failed with "button.challenge-button[value=\"{challenge_id}\"] does not match any elements" (challenge page requires CTFd login); flag correctness rests on the reproducible zbarimg decode, not on that recipe.
